evidence.quote: Term sheet: class fund $42,000,000; attorneys' fees $8,000,000; clear sailing no; unawarded fees revert to defendant no; distribution automatic
Term sheet: class fund $30,000,000; attorneys' fees $6,000,000; clear sailing yes; unawarded fees revert to defendant yes; distribution automatic
Attorneys’ fees were discussed alongside class-relief terms during negotiations, not only after class relief had been agreed.
any fee the court declines to award should augment the class recovery rather than return to Brightline
Hargrove’s opening demand is lower, so make one credible, all-in offer there while avoiding simultaneous binding settlements with both firms.
Accepting it meets Brightline’s authorization and is preferable to Hargrove Lane’s otherwise similar term sheet, which also removes clear sailing.

summary: Fees were included by both sides in the first negotiation round and were negotiated together with class relief before final settlement. The transcript links fee treatment to class recovery by requiring unawarded fees to augment the class fund. There is no evidence that class counsel prioritized its own economics over the class, especially because the transcript states fees did not affect counsel compensation. Defense did, however, shop between competing class counsel and selected the preferable parallel settlement term sheet.
